saints.name: St. Wulfstan of Worcester
saints.title: Bishop
saints.shortBlurb: The last Anglo-Saxon bishop, who kept his see through the Norman Conquest and fought the trade in slaves…
biography: Born about 1008 at Long Itchington in Warwickshire and schooled at the monasteries of Evesham and Peterborough, Wulfstan became a Benedictine monk of Worcester, where he served as treasurer and prior. In 1062 he was consecrated bishop of Worcester by Ealdred of York, having refused the hands of Stigand, whose own consecration was uncanonical.

After the Norman Conquest he alone of the English-born bishops kept his see, his holiness disarming the conquerors, and in 1075 he mustered the Worcestershire levies against the rebel earls. With Archbishop Lanfranc he broke up the trade by which the men of Bristol sold their English countrymen as slaves to Ireland, and he rebuilt his cathedral in stone, weeping as the old church came down.

He governed his diocese on horseback and on foot to the end, dying at Worcester in January 1095 while washing the feet of the poor, as was his custom. Miracles were reported at his tomb, and Innocent III canonized him in 1203. The city and diocese he served thirty-three years honor him as patron of Worcester.
saints.knownFor: Ending the Bristol slave trade and surviving the Conquest.
